Signs of the World

Pedestrian crossing

History

The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends a symbol of a walking pedestrian.

Adoption

The Vienna Convention lets each country choose a triangle or a diamond for its warning signs, and most of Europe chose the red-bordered triangle with a walking figure. The crossing underneath varies by country, drawn as dashed lines in the UK and Hong Kong and as stripes in Uganda. The United States, Canada, Mexico, New Zealand, Japan and most of Central and South America chose the black-on-yellow diamond. Australia is the standout with a pedestrian crossing sign that shows a pair of legs.
